study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative Modeling of Thalamic Nuclear Volumes and Characterization of Lateralized Volume Alterations in Alzheimer’s Disease Versus Schizophrenia

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Establish novel normative models of thalamic nuclear volumes and laterality indices from a large multi-cohort control sample, and apply these models to characterize alterations in Alzheimer’s disease and schizophrenia while linking deviations to clinical descriptors.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Pearson correlations between regional z-scores and clinical variables with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction; key finding includes association of the right medial dorsal nucleus with disorganized thought and daily auditory verbal hallucinations.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: AD shows larger and more symmetric thalamic nuclear volume reductions, while SCZ shows predominant right-sided thalamic involvement; right medial dorsal nucleus deviations relate to disorganized thought and daily auditory hallucinations.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Across nuclei, both SCZ and AD show leftward shifts in z-score distributions indicating reduced volumes, with strong overlap in pulvinar, medial dorsal, and centromedian nuclei; shifts are larger in AD. Laterality analyses suggest left-sided preference in EMCI and right-sided predilection in SCZ. Percent with at least one extreme deviation: Control infranormal 42.4%, supranormal 48.4%; EMCI 52.1%/52.6%; LMCI 67.3%/43.4%; AD 82.8%/33.3%; Early SCZ 49.4%/34.9%; UCLA SCZ 41.5%/41.5%; SCZ −AH 65.2%/52.2%; SCZ +AH 61.9%/42.9% (Supplemental Table 10).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: First normative models of thalamic laterality indices; utilization of HIPS-THOMAS on standard T1 MRI; systematic comparison of OLS, MFP, and GAMLSS; combined strategies for site effects (ComBat and hierarchical random effects); centile curves across lifespan.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Moderate normative reference sample size; relatively small SCZ cohorts; some thalamic nuclei absent from analyses; same model structure applied across regions; potential confounds (disease duration, substance use, medication burden, head motion) not addressed.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Controls aggregate to n=2374 with sex totals M=1095, F=1279 (46.1%/53.9%). ADNI treated as one site due to harmonized 3T Siemens protocol across 44 scanners. Overall control age range 5–100 years. MRI acquisition parameters per cohort are summarized (Supplementary Table 7).
